note: The most interesting ICP case in the batch, because he matches the aspirational half of the definition almost perfectly and was disqualified anyway. Successful is a clear match — technology sales, just closed a good quarter, held back to present internally, and when the rep guessed 'high-performer, business owner, executive' he answered 'That's true.' Good_to_great is a textbook match, confirmed in his own words when the rep framed it: 'we're not going back to the 10 out of 10 version of you, you want to go to the 12 out of 10 version.' Not_deconditioned is the strongest match in the whole corpus — 7-8% body fat six months ago, currently 12-13%, and the rep's own line was 'you're ripped, you've been ripped.' He misses on income as tested by affordability: three separate price rejections and a counter-anchor at $2,000-2,500 against a $4,000 tier, though as elsewhere in this folder no financial-picture questions were run, so this measures willingness rather than capacity. The material miss is neglected_health. Health is not this man's neglected area, it is his most developed one — eighteen months with a bodybuilding trainer, calisthenics coaching, basketball coaching, a carnivore phase and calorie tracking as routine. The stated ICP assumes health is the corner of a successful life that has been let go; here it is the corner that is already optimised, which is precisely why the rep concluded he did not need one-to-one coaching. That is a finding about the ICP, not about the rep: the criterion that screens people IN on profile screened this one OUT on need.
